hero.title: Duo Decide
hero.lead: A decision app for couples. One shared place to ask a question, vote or poll, and see it decided.

image.alt: Three screens from the Duo Decide design mock: the decision queue, poll rounds 2 and 3, and the create-decision sheet.

sections.title: Where it's at
paragraphs: Voting, three-round polls, option lists, history and real-time sync work on iOS and the web. The redesign shipped in October. November went to App Store readiness: an iOS 26 build, over-the-air updates, archive and soft delete, and a native accessibility pass.

expanders.title: What I'm building
paragraphs: One shared queue of decisions for two people. Vote mode is quick: one of you proposes options and the other picks. Poll mode is for harder calls: you both vote privately, it narrows to the two options you picked, and if you still disagree the partner who didn't start it makes the final pick.

expanders.title: What I tried
paragraphs: I split thinking from building. Ideas and trade-offs live in one repo, specs and code in another, and an idea moves over only once it is a decision. Every database migration is applied and tested in CI. Duo was also the first outside repo my AI pipeline worked on, and it opened real pull requests here.

expanders.title: What didn't work
paragraphs: My pipeline followed the voting doc to the letter, and the doc was wrong. It changed vote mode to wait for both partners, but the person who starts a vote can't vote on it. From July to October every vote-mode decision sat one step from done. The fix was to correct the doc first, then the code, plus a repair script for decisions already stuck. The pipeline behind it is my

Live testing found two more. A password-reset link signed people straight in instead of asking for a new password. And a deleted decision vanished from history for good, so deletes are now soft and decisions can be archived.

artifacts.title: One pick by the partner again
artifacts.text: The doc first, then the code, then a repair script for decisions already stuck. The tests that encoded the wrong rule now fail on the old code.

artifacts.title: Vote mode waits for both
artifacts.text: A pipeline run followed the voting doc. The person who starts a vote can't vote on it, so vote decisions stopped finishing.

artifacts.title: Soft delete
artifacts.text: A partner deleted a decision during live testing and it vanished from history. Migration 024 made deletes soft.

expanders.title: Open questions and next
paragraphs: Plan after deciding: once you pick a restaurant, add the time, place and notes, and keep it in history. Notifications for when your partner votes. Which tests and checks would let the pipeline merge a change without review. Then the App Store. One question is answered: who wins a split vote. In round 3 of a poll, the partner who didn't start it makes the final pick.
